title: Colorado River Salinity Control Fix Act
official_summary:
Colorado River Salinity Control Fix Act

This act modifies the Colorado River Basin Salinity Control Program to increase the federal cost share of salinity control projects that reduce the salt load in the Colorado River and other waters in the basin. The program supports salinity control projects or research in the (1) Upper Colorado River Basin in Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming; and (2) the Lower Colorado River Basin in Arizona, California, and Nevada. The program receives funding from appropriations for nonreimbursable costs and power revenues for reimbursable costs.

The act increases the percentages of nonreimbursable costs to increase support provided to the Lower Colorado River Basin.

summary.headline: New law raises the federal share of costs for projects that reduce salt in the Colorado River and its basin.
summary.what_it_does: This law changes the Colorado River Basin Salinity Control Program, which pays for projects and research that cut the amount of salt in the river and other waters in the basin. It raises the share of project costs that the federal government covers without being paid back. Those costs come from money Congress sets aside each year, while repaid costs come from power sales revenue. The change is meant to increase support for the Lower Colorado River Basin.

who_it_affects.group: Arizona, California, and Nevada (Lower Colorado River Basin)
who_it_affects.how: These states get more support because a larger part of salinity control costs no longer has to be repaid.

who_it_affects.group: Colorado, New Mexico, Utah, and Wyoming (Upper Colorado River Basin)
who_it_affects.how: Salinity control projects and research in these states are part of the program whose cost-sharing rules change.
The federal government takes on a larger share of salinity control project costs through yearly funding from Congress.

who_it_affects.group: Groups that pay power revenues into the program
who_it_affects.how: Less of the cost may need to be repaid through power revenues, since more is covered as federal cost that is not paid back.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; the summary does not give a separate start date.
